headline: Baseline, endpoint, and reference choices shape reported gains in biomedical ML
label: Biomedical Ml Evaluation Design Validity
summary: Recent preprints audit evaluation design itself, finding that baselines, degree-matching, and measurement models change which reported gains hold up.
synthesis: The common thread across these preprints is explicit sensitivity analysis of evaluation design. In noncoding RNA assays, sequence-model increments depend on the baseline chosen. In synthetic-lethality prediction, degree-matched AUROC and screen retrieval dissociate, with near-chance models still giving 2.62-fold enrichment. Transcriptomic similarity ranking adds signal beyond tissue matching when selecting source contexts for held-out drug responses. For Bayesian self-driving laboratories, a measurement-aware GP model with robust per-condition summaries and drift and day terms outperforms selection-level repairs in simulation. corrdeconv addresses a related confound, correcting deconvolution's treatment of disease cell states as abundance changes and validating against refutation tests. What is new is treating the evaluation contract itself, including baselines, controls, and measurement models, as a variable to be tested rather than fixed. The thread is dominant across these items but not universal to every study in the set.
